title: IMF Data Brief: Currency Composition of Official Foreign Exchange Reserves — World Aggregates, Q4 2025
date_evidence: Publication date: Mar 27, 2026 ... IMF Currency Composition of Official Foreign Exchange Reserves, World Aggregates, Fourth Quarter of 2025
key_claim: Total foreign exchange reserves rose to $13.14 trillion in 2025Q4; the US dollar share of allocated reserves edged down to 56.77 percent (from 56.93 percent in 2025Q3), the euro to 20.25 percent, while the Chinese renminbi rose to 1.95 percent and the residual 'other currencies' category — currencies not separately identified — increased to 6.13 percent from 5.61 percent, a share that began rising in 2021 and has since more than doubled.
notes: Tier 1 primary multilateral data. Anchors the gradual dollar-share drift and the rise of non-traditional reserve currencies. Read directly from IMF Data page; publication date Mar 27, 2026 shown on page.

title: The international role of the euro, June 2026
date_evidence: according to a European Central Bank report released Tuesday ... 'Geopolitical tensions continue to drive strong central bank demand for gold,' ECB President Christine Lagarde wrote in the report ... Taken from The European Central Bank report, June 2026 (reported by mining.com, 2 June 2026).
key_claim: Bullion accounted for 27 percent of global central-bank reserve assets at the end of 2025, up from 20 percent a year earlier, overtaking US Treasuries, which fell to 22 percent from 25 percent; euro-denominated reserves held at 15 percent and dollar-denominated assets remained the largest share at 42 percent; central banks hold more than 36,000 tonnes of gold; 2025 net buying eased to 850 tonnes after three years above 1,000 tonnes, with stablecoin issuer Tether the largest single buyer at more than 100 tonnes, while Turkey sold or loaned 130 tonnes in early 2026; ECB President Lagarde wrote that 'Geopolitical tensions continue to drive strong central bank demand for gold'.

notes: Tier 1 primary ECB document (annual 'international role of the euro' report). Cited inline alongside the mining.com reporting; treat as primary, corroborated.

title: Gold Demand Trends: Q1 2026 — Central Banks
date_evidence: Gold Demand Trends: Q1 2026 — Central Banks — 29 April, 2026
key_claim: Central bank net gold purchases were an estimated 244 tonnes in Q1 2026, up 17 percent quarter-on-quarter and above the five-year average; the National Bank of Poland (31t, to 582t) and the Central Bank of Uzbekistan (25t) led buying and the People's Bank of China added 7t (to 2,313t); reported sales rose to about 115t (Turkey around 70t, plus SOFAZ and Russia 22t each); unreported buying remained elevated, a trend in place since 2022.
notes: Tier 2 institutional data provider (WGC, data via Metals Focus; methodology disclosed). Anchors continued strong official-sector demand alongside an uptick in tactical sales. Read directly from page; publication date 29 April 2026.

title: Diversification enters a new phase
key_claim: Reserve diversification is 'entering a new phase' beyond gold itself: central banks continue to increase gold allocations amid sanctions risk and strategic resilience, but reserve managers — whose portfolios have become exceptionally large relative to domestic economies — are increasingly focused on liquidity, concentration risk, the future composition of safe assets and the long-term role of reserve currencies; the forthcoming Global Public Investor 2026 (launching 30 June) examines whether this is a structural reassessment of how public investors define safety, liquidity and capital preservation.
notes: Tier 2 institutional (Official Monetary and Financial Institutions Forum). Frames the analyst-voice claim that diversification has moved from composition to a structural reassessment of safety/custody. Read directly from page; meta published_time 29/05/2026.

title: Gold overtakes US Treasuries in global reserve shift: ECB
key_claim: Reporting the ECB's June 2026 report, gold reached 27 percent of global central-bank reserve assets at end-2025 (up from 20 percent) while US Treasuries fell to 22 percent (from 25 percent); the World Gold Council had said in January that gold held by foreign central banks was approaching $4 trillion, exceeding their roughly $3.9 trillion of US Treasuries — the first time foreign institutions held more gold than US government bonds since 1996; 2025 central-bank net buying eased to 850 tonnes, with Tether the largest single buyer at more than 100 tonnes and Turkey selling or loaning 130 tonnes in early 2026.
notes: Tier 3 specialist trade press; the verified carrier for the ECB June 2026 findings and the gold-vs-Treasuries crossover figures. Read directly from page; meta published_time 02/06/2026.

title: Why France Sold 129 Tonnes of Gold in New York, to Buy It Back in Europe? Inside BdF's Profitable Repatriation
key_claim: Between July 2025 and January 2026 the Banque de France sold 129 tonnes of older bullion (some dating to the late 1920s) held at the New York Fed and bought an equivalent volume of higher-standard LBMA-compliant bars in Europe, across 26 transactions, so that all 2,437 tonnes of France's gold (about 5 percent of which was the New York holding) are now stored in Paris; the operation booked a roughly £11.2 billion ($15 billion) gain and, as Governor Villeroy de Galhau stressed, was 'not politically motivated' but avoided physically shipping bars and the custody-withdrawal diplomacy seen in Germany's case.
notes: Tier 3 financial journalism. The canonical custody-relocation case (sell-old-in-NY, buy-new-in-Europe), illustrating repatriation executed without shipping or overt custody withdrawal. Read directly from page; byline and meta date 08/04/2026.

title: 'Our gold is no longer safe in the Fed's vaults' — German lawmakers and economists renew calls to repatriate sovereign gold
key_claim: German lawmakers and economists renewed calls to repatriate sovereign gold from the United States amid a rupture in transatlantic relations: of Germany's 3,350 tonnes of reserves (second only to the US), about 37 percent — 1,236 tonnes — is stored at the New York Fed, which a taxpayer-association head called 'no longer safe in the Fed's vaults'; the ruling CDU and Bundesbank President Nagel resisted, citing 'no cause for concern', but the episode revived the access-versus-custody distinction, following Germany's 2013-2020 repatriation of 300 tonnes from New York and 374 tonnes from Paris; the New York Fed remains the world's largest gold custodian, holding about 6,300 tonnes for more than 30 central banks.
verbatim_quote: no longer safe in the Fed's vaults
notes: Tier 3 specialist news. STRUCTURAL ANCHOR (3-6m band, 26/01/2026): canonical framing of the custody-trust signal (German debate; NY Fed concentration; access-vs-custody). Date read from visible byline and URL stamp.
